description:
Found by cold review of fz-5xp.15, which added the fifth copy.

    if bytes.len() > SHARED_BIN_THRESHOLD_BYTES {
        heap_ref_word(ValueKind::PROCBIN, p)
    } else {
        heap_ref_word(ValueKind::BITSTRING, p)
    }

appears in runtime/src/ir_runtime.rs at `fz_bs_finalize`, `fz_binary_concat`,
`fz_alloc_bitstring_const`, and now `alloc_text` -- over a
`Heap::alloc_bitstring` (runtime/src/heap/imp.rs) that ALREADY branches on the
same threshold to decide what it allocated. So the decision is made once inside
the heap and then re-derived by every caller from the byte length.

fz-5xp.15 added `alloc_text` as a shared helper for its three new primitives,
which was the right instinct and the wrong scope: it folded three future copies
and left the four existing ones alone.

DONE = `Heap::alloc_bitstring` returns the tagged word, and no caller decides
`PROCBIN` vs `BITSTRING` again. One question, one implementation -- and the
threshold stops being a constant that four call sites have to agree about.
title: The inline-bitstring vs shared-procbin choice is written five times
